Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

collection noun

things collected and kept

also collections, a stamp collection, a coin collection, an art collection, collector

modern

M-O s.v. collection (marked as a modern sense)

collēctiō, collēctiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a collection

Classically the act of gathering (Cic. Imp. Pomp. 22: membrōrum collēctiō), a summing-up in rhetoric and, in medicine, a swelling or abscess (Lewis & Short); the sense “things collected” is modern. A Roman named the things themselves, signa, tabulae, nummī, with colligere (see collect).

Other words

  • thēsaurus, thēsaurī m. — a store, a treasure laid up

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 21 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. collection

    A hoard or store of valuable things; of a collection, a treasure of them.

  • corpus, corporis n. — a collection of writings, a body of texts

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 3.34.7: corpus omnis Rōmānī jūris (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. collection

    The whole body of a set of writings or laws; first of all a body.

  • dactyliothēca, dactyliothēcae f. — a collection of rings and gems

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plin. NH 37.11

    A Greek word for a ring box (Mart. 11.59.4), which Pliny uses of a collection of gems.

Examples

  • Gemmās plūrēs prīmus omnium Rōmae habuit — quod peregrīnō appellant nōmine dactyliothēcam — prīvignus Sullae Scaurus

    The first man at Rome to own a collection of gems (they call it by a foreign name, a dactyliotheca) was Sulla’s stepson ScaurusPlin. NH 37.11

See also collect, museum, coin, stamp.
